title: Mouse Trap

beats.what: Jim heard the Thomas voice; rushes outside and finds children fine but is shaken
Boyd reveals plan to catch a creature; Donna opposes it as reckless grief-rage
Boyd and Kenny's foraging group reaches the lake settlement with statues and old talismans
Jade fights with Dale and the others; storms off from foraging party
Boyd walks alongside the memory board he is building -- names of the dead
Jade trapped in old bear trap; Kristi and Kenny work to free her as dark approaches
Tabitha and Henry arrive at the park; Tabitha sees the bottle tree and has a crisis of reality
Ethan directly asks Jim who will bury Mom if she is dead outside
Fatima opens up to Tillie about her terror of something being wrong with the baby
Henry drives Tabitha to the park tree -- car accident on the road back into town begins

character_beats.beat: wants to honor the dead through purposeful action rather than grief paralysis; designs a creature-capture plan while building a memory board -- two forms of doing that mask an inability to simply feel the loss
wants to return to his obsession at the bar rather than do communal labor; abandons the group, gets trapped, and has to be saved by the same people he dismissed
wants to trust that the outside world is real; the moment she sees Miranda's necklace in a car near the park, she breaks down -- convinced the place is still staging her reality

key_lines.line: Those things said they wanted to break you, and that means they wanted to change you.
key_lines.why: Frames Boyd's offensive pivot as the very behavior the creatures engineered

key_lines.line: We can't just sit around playing it safe anymore.
key_lines.why: Boyd's stated rationale for the capture plan; echoes through the episode's action

key_lines.line: You'll never be alone, okay? You're gonna be fine.
key_lines.why: Kristi to Kenny, invoking Tian-Chen's dying message; links grief to forward motion

key_lines.line: No matter what this place throws at us, we are going to find our way home.
key_lines.why: Boyd to Donna's son -- defiant promise made as the episode's crisis accelerates

open_loops: What triggered the car crash on the road to the park -- is the place preventing Tabitha from reaching the tree?
What were the ancient talismans at the lake settlement doing, and who placed them?
Will the creature-capture plan work, and what will it cost?
What exactly is wrong with Fatima's pregnancy that she cannot speak aloud?

payoffs.what: Henry takes Tabitha to the park with Miranda's bottle tree -- the physical location finally reached

contradiction.wants: to leave the foraging party and return to his private obsession, framing it as being 'more helpful back in town'
contradiction.does: abandons the group in the forest and immediately gets caught in a trap, requiring rescue from the people he just abandoned

tone_notes: This episode has three major silence pockets: 144 seconds (~04:08-06:32), 104 seconds (~13:04-14:48), and 71 seconds (~27:39-28:51). The first two sit around Jim's Thomas-voice paranoia and the approach to the lake settlement -- both dread-build pauses. The 144-second gap is the season's second-longest. Density peaks at minutes 30 and 31 (200 and 124 words/min) -- the exact trap sequence and its aftermath. At 96.9 words/min average this is the most verbally dense of the five hours, suggesting a script that rarely lets characters breathe.
